name: Tbilisi
notes: capital, National Bank of Georgia, Bank of Georgia and TBC Bank, government, Georgian Railway, Rose Revolution (2003), Middle Corridor freight and logistics offices

name: Batumi-Adjara
notes: Batumi port and oil terminal (Kazakh and Turkmen oil by rail), casinos and Turkish tourists, Sarpi crossing to Turkey, Supsa oil terminal (Baku-Supsa pipeline) in Guria, Kobuleti

name: Abkhazia
notes: Sukhumi, Gagra resorts for Russian tourists, Russian base at Gudauta, Ochamchire port, citrus, the Enguri dam's power station at Gali; recognized by Russia since the 2008 war

name: Kutaisi-Poti
notes: Kutaisi (low-cost airport), Poti port and free zone, Kulevi oil terminal (SOCAR), Enguri dam, Chiatura manganese and Zestaponi ferroalloys (Georgian Manganese), Anaklia deep-sea port (cancelled January 2020), Svaneti

name: Rustavi-Kakheti
notes: Rustavi steel and fertilizer, Madneuli copper-gold mine at Bolnisi (RMG), Marneuli's Azerbaijani farms, Kakheti wine (Telavi, Kvareli), the Pankisi gorge, Red Bridge crossing to Azerbaijan

name: Gori-Borjomi
notes: Gori (Stalin's birthplace), Mtskheta, Gudauri ski slopes and the Upper Lars road to Russia (the only open land crossing), Borjomi mineral water, Akhaltsikhe, Armenian-majority Javakheti, Baku-Tbilisi-Kars railway (2017)

name: South Ossetia
notes: Tskhinvali, Russian base and troops, taken by Russia in the 2008 five-day war (19-history), Roki tunnel to North Ossetia, Akhalgori; "borderization" fences creep into Georgian villages

name: Yerevan
notes: capital, Central Bank, Pashinyan's government after the 2018 Velvet Revolution, diaspora money, IT and chip design offices (Synopsys Armenia), Ararat brandy, Russian-owned power and gas grids

name: Ararat-Armavir
notes: Metsamor nuclear plant (about 40% of power), Echmiadzin (seat of the Armenian Church), Zvartnots airport, Ararat valley apricots, grapes and brandy; closed Turkish border

name: Kotayk-Gegharkunik
notes: Lake Sevan, Hrazdan power plant (Russian-owned), Sotk gold mine near the Azerbaijani line, Tsaghkadzor ski resort, Abovyan

name: Shirak-Aragatsotn
notes: Gyumri (Russia's 102nd military base), 1988 Spitak earthquake zone, Mount Aragats and Byurakan observatory, closed rail line to Kars

name: Lori-Tavush
notes: Vanadzor chemicals, Alaverdi copper smelter, Teghut copper-molybdenum mine, Dilijan (Central Bank training centre), Tavush border with Azerbaijan (sniper fire)

name: Syunik-Vayots Dzor
notes: Zangezur Copper Molybdenum Combine at Kajaran (Armenia's biggest exporter and taxpayer), Kapan gold, Jermuk mineral water, Meghri crossing to Iran, Goris and the Lachin road to Nagorno-Karabakh

name: Baku
notes: capital, SOCAR and the State Oil Fund (SOFAZ), Central Bank, Bibi-Heybat and Absheron oil, Sangachal terminal (start of the BTC oil and South Caucasus gas pipelines; BP-led ACG and Shah Deniz offshore), Alat port (Middle Corridor), Baku shipyard, F1 street race

name: Sumgait-Shamakhi
notes: Sumgait petrochemicals (SOCAR Polymer, 2018; Azerikimya), aluminium and pipe plants, Absheron dachas, Shamakhi wine and observatory, Ismayilli

name: Ganja-Gazakh
notes: Ganja (second city, aluminium plant), Gadabay gold (Anglo Asian Mining), Dashkasan iron ore, Naftalan oil spa, Gazakh and Tovuz on the Georgian and Armenian borders (BTC route, border shooting)

name: Shaki-Zagatala
notes: Shaki khans' palace, hazelnuts (a top world exporter), tobacco and silk, Zagatala, Gabala (former Russian radar), Georgian border

name: Guba-Khachmaz
notes: Guba apples, Khachmaz, Siyazan oil, Samur crossing to Russia (rail and road north), Shahdag ski resort, Caspian beaches

name: Mingachevir-Shirvan
notes: Mingachevir dam and power plant (the biggest in the South Caucasus), Yevlakh rail junction, Shirvan, Barda, cotton

name: Mil-Mughan-Salyan
notes: cotton and grain at Saatly, Sabirabad and Imishli, Kura and Araz rivers, Salyan and Neftchala oil fields, Iran border; Beylagan and Aghjabadi near the Karabakh line

name: Lankaran
notes: tea, citrus and vegetables, Astara crossing to Iran (North-South transport corridor rail), Talysh mountains, Caspian coast

name: Nakhchivan
notes: exclave between Armenia, Iran and Turkey, Aliyev family homeland, Sadarak crossing to Turkey, salt mines, blockaded by Armenia since the 1990s

name: Nagorno-Karabakh
notes: run by the Armenian-backed Artsakh Republic since the 1994 ceasefire: Stepanakert, Shusha, Drmbon gold-copper mine, plus the seven surrounding Azerbaijani districts emptied in the war (Kalbajar, Lachin, Aghdam and others) (A), Lachin corridor to Armenia, line of contact (2016 April war)
